description: National Climate Assessment (Fifth) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USGCRP, U.S. Global Change Research Program. Released in 2023, this report is the U.S. Government’s preeminent report on climate change impacts, risks, and responses. It is a congressionally mandated interagency effort that provides the scientific foundation to support informed decision-making across the United States. USGCRP. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Changing Seasons, Drought, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – General, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease, Water Quality, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Aquatic and Marine Resources, Economy, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
